correctness.rationale: Lee–Kim Proposition 2/Remark 1 reduce the global finite-exchangeable problem to the max over hypergeometric population count k, sample size m, and real tilt t; symmetry reduces k,m <= floor(N/2). For Bernoulli reductions use sharp Kearns–Saul constant, giving 1/log(2) at N=3 and 1/[2log(3/2)] at N=5. For N=4, the k=m=2 hypergeometric MGF (2+cosh t)/3 <= exp(t^2/6) by nonnegative series coefficients, while an m=1 balanced Bernoulli attains 4/3 in the variance limit. For N=5 k=m=2, differentiation gives variance 6u(u²+2u+3)/(u²+6u+3)² maximized at sqrt(3) with bound 5(sqrt(3)-1)/3 < 1/[2log(3/2)]; remaining small pairs are dominated. For N=6, explicit rational nonnegative tilted-variance certificates for (k,m)=(2,2),(2,3),(3,3) and Bernoulli k=1 prove <=6/5, attained by k=3,m=1 as t tends to zero. The entire range of real tilts follows by double integration of variance; no finite numerical search is used as infinite proof. Independent symbolic simplification checked all three N6 identities and the N5 derivative identity from the source package.
